title: K-Nearest Neighbors & Support Vector Machines — Choose K and the Margin
key_insight: K controls that balance. For an SVM, the margin is the safety gap, and a penalty setting decides how much to bend the rule for misclassified training points.
body:
## Choose K and the Margin

One nearest neighbor can copy a noisy label, while too many neighbors can wash away a small local group.

K controls that balance. For an SVM, the margin is the safety gap, and a penalty setting decides how much to bend the rule for misclassified training points.

Choose these settings with validation. KNN stores the examples; an SVM stores the boundary-defining support vectors.
common_mistakes: Using either method before scaling features.
Choosing K or kernel settings on the test set.
Assuming KNN training is costly while ignoring its prediction-time search.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Choose K and the Margin” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: These contrasting methods teach how distance, boundaries, and scaling shape classification.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Choose K and the Margin” story, explain K-Nearest Neighbors & Support Vector Machines without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
